Liquid AI has released LFM2.5-2.6B, a 2.6-billion parameter open-weights model specifically engineered for on-device agentic AI deployment on extremely resource-constrained hardware including Raspberry Pi and other edge devices. The model supports a 128K context window and includes native tool-calling capabilities—features previously thought impossible at this scale without cloud infrastructure or dedicated accelerators.

This release represents a significant breakthrough for local LLM practitioners working with embedded systems and IoT deployments. The ability to run agentic models directly on sub-$50 hardware eliminates latency concerns, removes cloud dependency, and enables truly offline-first AI applications. The open-weights approach also means developers can fine-tune and customize the model for specific use cases without vendor lock-in.

For teams deploying AI across distributed edge networks, agriculture sensors, or remote locations with unreliable connectivity, this model class removes previous technical barriers. The focus on practical agent capabilities (tool calling, reasoning, context retention) over raw performance metrics makes LFM2.5-2.6B immediately actionable for production edge deployments.
